title: Generation of multicomponent Schrödinger cat states in schemes with measurement of Gaussian states
authors: E. A. Nesterova, S. B. Korolev
abstract: In this work, we propose a scheme for generating superpositions of Fock states whose numbers differ by four or eight. The proposed protocol is based on photon-number-resolving measurements on multimode Gaussian states. We compare of the generated states with multicomponent Schrödinger cat states. We evaluate the fidelity and determine how it scales with the number of detected particles. Furthermore, we derive the optimal configuration for the generation such states.
summary: This paper details a quantum optical protocol for generating high-fidelity multicomponent Schrödinger cat states (e.g., 4-state, 8-state) by measuring photon numbers in multimode Gaussian states. The scheme uses squeezed vacuum states and beam splitters, demonstrating that fidelity can approach theoretical limits, although the probability of generating higher-order states decreases rapidly.
main_problem: The paper proposes a probabilistic scheme to generate high-fidelity multicomponent Schrödinger cat states, specifically focusing on 4-component and 8-component superpositions.
main_result: The scheme successfully generates states approximating the target cat states with fidelities approaching the theoretical maximum, although the generation probability decreases rapidly for higher components.
method: The generation relies on performing photon-number-resolving measurements on multimode Gaussian states, which are prepared using squeezed vacuum states and beam splitters.
model_or_system: The system involves multimode Gaussian states, which are manipulated using linear optical elements (beam splitters) and measured using Photon-Number-Resolving Detectors (PNRDs). The target states are superpositions of Fock states, known as Schrödinger cat states.
key_observables: Fidelity ($\mathcal{F}$), generation probability ($\mathcal{P}$), and the expansion coefficients of the generated state across Fock number basis states.
important_parameters: The state is characterized by parameters $A$ and $B$ for 4-states, and the process involves optimizing over several physical parameters $\{r_1, r_2, t_1, t_2, \phi\}$ and the coherent state amplitude $ eta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to perform PNR measurements and relies on deriving the optimal parameter configurations to maximize fidelity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the generation schemes (e.g., using two pairs of squeezed states for 4-states) and compare the achieved fidelity ($\mathcal{F}$) against the theoretical maximum ($\mathcal{F}_{	ext{max}}$) as a function of the number of superposition terms ($p$).
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the general scheme for 4-states using PNR measurements on Gaussian states. It then details a specialized, optimized scheme for 4-states, followed by the extension to 8-states by mixing two 4-states. Finally, it discusses the recursive generalization to higher-order states and analyzes the trade-off between fidelity and generation probability.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, experimentally relevant protocol for creating complex quantum states (cat states) that are highly sought after for quantum computation and quantum metrology, directly linking measurement theory to state preparation.
